skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - explain why it's important to communicate technical concepts in non-technical language - explain the types of communication that can be used with internal and external stakeholders, and their impact
You can: - interpret data to find key insights

You can: - develop a basic understanding of an unfamiliar or emerging technology, or a familiar technology in a new data context, with guidance - share what you learn with colleagues, including how it could help deliver more value from data
You can: - show an awareness of different data models and tools, and understand when they could be used - show an awareness of industry-recognised data modelling patterns and standards
You can: - explain what metadata is - maintain the information stored in metadata repositories under the direction of others

You can: - investigate problems in systems, processes and services, with an understanding of the level of a problem, for example, strategic, tactical or operational - contribute to the implementation of remedies and preventative measures
You can: - correctly execute test scripts under supervision - understand the role of testing and how it works

skill: Turning business problems into data design
expected_level_description: You can: - contribute to the design of data architecture under the direction of others
You can: - describe the main parts of the health and care system and the services the organisation supports - explain why patient safety and confidentiality matter in your work
You can: - follow the organisation's rules for handling personal and health information - recognise and report a data breach or near miss
You can: - explain why accurate health data matters for care and planning - record data accurately and report errors
You can: - explain the difference between a clinical terminology and a classification - recognise common terminologies such as SNOMED CT and ICD
